original_question: For Linton's 1976 two-unit parallel redundant system with state probabilities q0,i(x,t), q1,i(x,t), and q2,j(x,t), where one unit has k failure stages, the other has m repair phases, the boundary condition includes q0,1(0,t) = integral from 0 to infinity of q1,1(x,t) g(x) dx + delta(t), lambda > 0 and mu > 0 are system parameters, g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1, and f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2, determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution when g(x) and f(x) are non-constant functions.
target_in_paper: The nearest paper-faithful target is the paper’s final open-problem direction, as identified in the abstract: for the stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times, move beyond the constant-rate case and the general-case Laplace-transform treatment to determine the general nonconstant-rate time-dependent solution and its long-time behavior, in the nonautonomous evolution-family formulation.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly points toward a PDE reliability-type model, asks about well-posedness and asymptotic behavior, and focuses on the harder nonconstant-rate case rather than the already-solved constant-rate regime. Those features are genuinely close to the paper’s open-problem direction.
missing_details: The inspected paper is not about Linton’s 1976 two-unit parallel redundant system; it studies a stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times.

The draft introduces unrelated state variables q0,i(x,t), q1,i(x,t), q2,j(x,t), the boundary condition q0,1(0,t)=∫_0^∞ q1,1(x,t)g(x)dx+δ(t), and parameters λ, μ, g, f from a different model; these should be removed.
The paper’s rate data are the job-dependent processing rate, up-time rate, and repair rate; the draft should name those, rather than only two functions g(x) and f(x).

The paper explicitly contrasts two regimes: the constant-rate case, where the time-dependent solution is obtained explicitly and its asymptotic behavior is derived, and the general nonconstant-rate case, where only the Laplace transform is obtained. That contrast is essential to the paper’s intent.

The PDE system in the paper is said to contain Dirac-delta functions in both the boundary and the initial conditions; that structural feature should be stated at the level of the paper’s model, not via an imported boundary condition from another system.

The paper states that C_0-semigroup theory is not suitable for this model; if 'well posedness' is asked for, it should be posed in the nonautonomous abstract Cauchy problem/evolution-family setting, not as a standard C_0-semigroup question.
The paper reformulates the model as an abstract Cauchy problem whose underlying operator is an evolution family; that reformulation is part of the intended scope and should be included.
The draft should not ask about a broader neighboring reliability system; it should stay narrowly with the scheduling model and its general nonconstant-rate case.

Algebraic metadata such as ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, and nilpotency are not applicable here; the missing structural data instead concern the operator-theoretic framework, the nonautonomous nature of the problem, and the relevant rate functions.
refined_question: For the stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times, described by a system of partial differential equations with Dirac-delta terms in the boundary and initial conditions, and in the general case where the job-dependent processing rate, up-time rate, and repair rate are nonconstant functions, can one establish well-posedness of the resulting nonautonomous abstract Cauchy problem in the evolution-family framework, recover the actual time-dependent solution (rather than only its Laplace transform), and determine its long-time asymptotic behavior?
equivalent_formulation: After rewriting the PDE system as an abstract Cauchy problem whose underlying operator is an evolution family rather than a C_0-semigroup, determine in the general nonconstant-rate case whether the problem is well posed and characterize both the time-dependent solution and its asymptotic behavior.
justification: The draft overlaps with the paper only at the level of asking about PDE well-posedness/asymptotics for a nonconstant-rate reliability model. However, the specific model in the draft is not the one studied in arXiv:2405.11510. The paper’s abstract states that the paper studies a stochastic scheduling model on an unreliable machine with general up-times and general set-up times; solves the constant-rate case explicitly and asymptotically; obtains only the Laplace transform in the general case; shows that C_0-semigroup theory is not suitable; reformulates the model as an abstract Cauchy problem governed by an evolution family; and finally leaves open problems. So the sharpest stand-alone reformulation closest to the paper is the unresolved general-case question about well-posedness/time-dependent solution/asymptotics in that evolution-family setting, not the unrelated Linton parallel-redundancy model.
